title: IntentDoc
description: One suss intent document, either boundary intent or a PRD, see https://github.com/nimbuscloud-ai/suss/blob/main/docs/reference/intent-format.md

kind.description: Makes this document boundary intent for one boundary.

name.description: What this document is called. A PRD scenario links to an outcome of it as <name>.<outcome-id>.

purpose.description: What the boundary is for, in the author's own words.

audience.description: Who calls this boundary and depends on what it does.

source.description: Where the document came from: somebody wrote it, suss inferred it, or suss inferred it and somebody has since curated it.

method.description: The HTTP method the route handles.

path.description: The route path, written the way the framework declares it.

required.description: Whether the boundary needs this field.

headers.description: The request headers the boundary depends on, by name.

required.description: Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.

query.description: The query-string parameters the boundary depends on, by name.

required.description: Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.

params.description: The path parameters the boundary depends on, by name.

body.description: The shape of the request body the boundary depends on.

receives.description: The parts of the request the boundary depends on.

module.description: The repo-relative module path, when the boundary is a unit inside this repository.

exportName.description: The name the module or package exports the function under.

package.description: The package name, when the boundary is something a package publishes.

exportPath.description: The path to the export inside the package: the sub-path, then any nested names.

required.description: Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.

receives.description: The fields the boundary is handed, by field name. On a function-call boundary a name is a parameter, on a message bus it is a field of the message body.

messageBus.description: Which bus carries the message, in the name suss gives that bus.

channel.description: The queue or topic the message travels on. Null when the document does not name one.

required.description: Whether the boundary needs this field.

Whether the boundary needs this field.

receives.description: The fields the boundary is handed, by field name. On a function-call boundary a name is a parameter, on a message bus it is a field of the message body.

storageSystem.description: Which store this is: postgresql, aws.dynamodb, s3, and so on.

scope.description: The ORM, schema or deployment scope the container is in. A setup with one database uses default.

container.description: The table, bucket, collection or index. Null when the document does not name one.

accessPath.description: A secondary way into the container, such as a DynamoDB index or an Elasticsearch alias. Null means the container's own primary way in.

required.description: Whether the boundary needs this field.

Whether the boundary needs this field.

receives.description: The fields the boundary is handed, by field name. On a function-call boundary a name is a parameter, on a message bus it is a field of the message body.

deploymentTarget.description: What sort of deployed thing this is: a Lambda function, an ECS task's container, a plain container, a k8s deployment or an edge worker.

instanceName.description: The name the deployment medium knows the unit by, such as a CloudFormation logical id. Null when the document does not name one.

required.description: Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.
Whether the boundary needs this field.

receives.description: The fields the boundary is handed, by field name. On a function-call boundary a name is a parameter, on a message bus it is a field of the message body.

boundary.description: Which boundary in the code the document is about.

id.description: The outcome's name. A PRD scenario links to it as <intent-name>.<id>.

when.description: What has to hold for this outcome, either as a list of clauses or as one sentence.

response.description: This outcome sends an HTTP response.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response carries.

body.description: The shape of the response body.

returns.description: This outcome returns a value to its caller.

body.description: The shape of the returned value.

errorType.description: The name of the error class this outcome raises.

results.description: The effects this outcome has, written in the same verbs suss ask uses: reads, writes, invokes.

transitions.description: Every outcome the boundary can produce, one entry each.

kind.description: Makes this document a PRD, a set of scenarios for a feature.

purpose.description: What the feature is for, in the author's own words.

source.description: Where the document came from: somebody wrote it, suss inferred it, or suss inferred it and somebody has since curated it.

title.description: A short name for the scenario.

when.description: The condition the scenario covers, in the author's own words.

expect.description: What should happen then, in the author's own words.

link.description: The boundary-intent outcomes this scenario is about, each written <intent-name>.<outcome-id>.

scenarios.description: The situations the feature covers, one entry each.
